mission_05: Optical computing uses light instead of electricity for computation, offering potentially ultra-low latency and energy-efficient matrix operations. Mach-Zehnder Interferometers (MZIs) are the building blocks: they split light into two paths, apply phase shifts, and recombine to implement 2x2 unitary transformations. By arranging MZIs in a mesh (Clements decomposition), any NxN unitary matrix can be implemented optically. Matrix multiplication uses SVD decomposition: W = U @ S @ V^T, where U and V^T are implemented as optical unitary transformations and S is applied via programmable attenuators. In this mission, you implement MZI transfer matrices, an optical mesh that applies unitary transformations, SVD-based matrix multiplication decomposition, and power efficiency calculation for optical computation.
